label: RESEARCH CONTEXT
description: Hand-verified public writing from four venture firms, used as RESEARCH CONTEXT in Thesis Court. These are not treated or scored as predictions, and are not records of the firms' investment decisions. Quotes are verbatim from the live page (accessed_at) and from the archive capture (archived_url). Thesis summaries and hypotheses are curator paraphrases; each item's thesis_review holds the finance owner's review note (Yaseen, 2026-11-13).

items.title: Link Ventures | Backing AI founders from MIT, Harvard, and beyond
items.published_at_basis: NOT AVAILABLE: living firm home page with no publication date on the page (footer shows only '© 2025 Link Ventures').
items.available_at_basis: Earliest Wayback Machine capture we checked (roughly monthly captures, 2025-02 to 2026-10) that contains every quote below verbatim. Earlier captures used different wording: the 2025-03-05 capture reads 'a venture capital firm that is based in Kendall Square, just a block from MIT, that invests in technical founders developing disruptive AI technologies', and the 2025-06-17 to 2025-08-09 captures contain the first quote but not the other two. Only those captures were checked, so the current text may have appeared somewhat before 2025-09-14; the date is conservative.
items.thesis: Link Ventures says it invests at pre-seed, seed and Series A in technical founders, especially from MIT, Harvard and the Boston ecosystem, who build AI companies. It says it pairs capital with hands-on operating support and shared resources (office space, housing, payroll, data, compute, accounting, legal) that free founders to build. As a lens: technical depth plus shared operating infrastructure is presented as the way to scale an AI startup. Separately, and with no supporting data on the page, it claims that using machine learning to scale startups saves time and capital.
items.thesis_review: Reviewed by Yaseen (2026-11-13): Checked on 2026-11-13 against the live page and the archive capture: all 3 quotes appear verbatim on both. Thesis edited: the earlier text tied 'saving time and capital' to the shared back-office support, but the page attaches that claim to 'using machine learning to scale startups'; the two are now stated separately. Also aligned to the page's wording ('pre-seed, seed and Series A', 'especially from MIT and Harvard') and its full list of shared resources. Hypotheses unchanged (labelled curator-derived). Quote kinds: all 3 confirmed as classified. Limitation: this checks the summary against the page text only; it does not verify the firm's claims.
hypotheses: Curator-derived, not a firm claim: technically deep founding teams with access to shared operating infrastructure (compute, payroll, legal, accounting) carry lower early operational execution risk.
Curator-derived, not a firm claim: using AI/ML inside a startup's own operations lets it scale with less time and capital than a conventional build-out.

quotes.text: Link Ventures is a venture capital firm based in Kendall Square, just a block from MIT and Harvard, that invests in technical founders developing disruptive AI technologies.

We invest in top technical founders from MIT, Harvard, and Boston’s ecosystem building impactful AI solutions. Our focus is on scalable models, data-driven products, and disruptive innovation with global potential.
quotes.note: Stated investment criteria (what the firm says it looks for), not evidence of outcomes.

quotes.text: Link Ventures fuels AI-driven innovation, using machine learning to scale startups into market leaders—saving time and capital while building enduring value.
quotes.note: Promotional claim; no supporting data on the page.

limitations: A firm home page is marketing copy, not research; it is persuasive writing, not a calibrated forecast.
No publication date on the page; availability for replay is established only from archive captures.
Living page: wording can change at any time. Quotes were confirmed on the live page on accessed_at and in the archived capture.
Says nothing about rejected investments, realized returns, or fund performance.

items.title: Portfolio | Link Ventures
items.published_at_basis: NOT AVAILABLE: living portfolio page. The Silverton Power and Spinor Energy entries show 'Year Invested 2026' but no exact date.
items.available_at_basis: Earliest Wayback Machine capture we checked that contains every quote below. The 2026-06-09 capture did not contain the Silverton Power or Spinor Energy entries.
items.thesis: Two 2026 entries on Link's portfolio page (Silverton Power, Spinor Energy) describe electric power as a constraint on AI build-out. Silverton's entry calls speed to power the binding constraint on the U.S. economy, saying the years-long wait to energize new load gates everything from AI to advanced manufacturing. Spinor's entry describes the megawatt-per-millisecond load swings of gigawatt-scale AI training campuses as a pain point its storage product addresses. The entries have no stated author and may be company-supplied. As a curator lens: AI-first businesses depend critically on physical infrastructure (grid power) whose lead times sit outside the company's control.
items.thesis_review: Reviewed by Yaseen (2026-11-13): Checked on 2026-11-13 against the live page and the archive capture: both quotes appear verbatim on both. Thesis edited: the earlier text said both entries call power 'a binding constraint on AI data-center build-out'; only Silverton uses 'binding constraint', and it applies it to the U.S. economy broadly, while Spinor describes AI load swings as a pain point. Each entry is now summarized separately, the lens sentence is marked as the curator's, and the no-stated-author caveat is added because the thesis is shown without the limitations list. Second hypothesis: 'on-grid storage' changed to 'grid-side and behind-the-meter storage', because Silverton deploys batteries on the distribution grid and Spinor's product is behind-the-meter. Quote kinds: both confirmed as classified. Limitation: this checks the summary against the page text only; it does not verify the companies' claims.
hypotheses: Curator-derived, not a firm claim: for a business whose growth needs new compute or data-center capacity, grid interconnection lead time is a critical dependency that can delay revenue and extend cash burn.
Curator-derived, not a firm claim: power-delivery bottlenecks create demand for grid-side and behind-the-meter storage and load-smoothing products.

quotes.text: Speed to power has become the binding constraint on the U.S. economy - the years-long wait to energize new load now gates everything from AI to advanced manufacturing - and Silverton is solving it with renewable power.
quotes.note: From the Silverton Power portfolio entry. The page does not say who wrote the entry.

quotes.text: Its near-term product is a behind-the-meter “shock absorber” that smooths the megawatt-per-millisecond load swings created by gigawatt-scale AI training campuses
quotes.note: Product description from the Spinor Energy portfolio entry (sentence continues on the page). Describes the product as stated; not an independent technical verification.

limitations: A portfolio page is not a record of rejected investments or realized returns; it lists companies the firm chose to show.

Entry text has no stated author. Some entries on the same page are written in the first person by the company (e.g. Darwin Robotics), so blurbs may be company-supplied rather than Link's own analysis.
Only 'Year Invested' is shown, not a transaction date or terms.
Living page; entries were added between the 2026-06-09 and 2026-10-05 captures.

items.title: Fintech Investments, Team, & Thesis Overview | a16z
items.published_at_basis: NOT AVAILABLE as a visible date. Page metadata (JSON-LD) says datePublished 2023-04-11T07:25:18+00:00 and dateModified 2026-11-10T16:52:15+00:00, which date the page, not the current wording of the quoted paragraph.
items.available_at_basis: Earliest Wayback Machine capture we checked that contains the current wording of every quote below. The 2023-05-09 capture had an earlier version ('mobile, digital money, machine learning, and new data sources ... reimagine the way we manage our finances'); the 2023-08-30 capture did not contain the current wording.
items.thesis: a16z's fintech team says fintech companies are innovating across banking, lending, insurance, real estate and investing, in both customer-facing products and core infrastructure. It states a belief that the combination of mobile, digital money, AI and machine learning, and new data sources gives startups an opportunity to leapfrog outdated infrastructure and compete with incumbent financial institutions.
items.thesis_review: Reviewed by Yaseen (2026-11-13): Checked on 2026-11-13 against the live page and the archive capture: both quotes appear verbatim on both. Thesis edited for precision: the earlier text stated as fact that startups 'can' leapfrog, while the page frames it as a belief ('We believe ... offers startups a unique opportunity'); it also merged the page's description of where fintech companies innovate with the belief. The two are now separate. Hypotheses unchanged (labelled curator-derived). Quote kinds: both confirmed as analyst_interpretation; the first (a general description of the market with no data) is borderline with documentary_fact. Limitation: this checks the summary against the page text only.
hypotheses: Curator-derived, not a firm claim: incumbents' outdated infrastructure is an operational bottleneck that new entrants can exploit.
Curator-derived, not a firm claim: core financial infrastructure, not only customer-facing apps, is a place where new entrants compete.

quotes.text: Fintech companies are innovating across broad categories—in banking, lending, insurance, real estate, and investing—both on the customer-facing side and in core infrastructure.
quotes.note: General characterization of the market; no data given.

quotes.text: We believe the combination of mobile, digital money, AI and machine learning, and new data sources offers startups a unique opportunity to leapfrog outdated infrastructure and compete with incumbent financial institutions to reimagine the way money moves.
quotes.note: Explicit belief statement (thesis), not a measurable forecast.

limitations: Persuasive thesis writing, not a calibrated numerical forecast; contains no testable numeric prediction.
Living hub page: the thesis paragraph's wording changed between the 2023-05-09 and 2023-11-26 captures, so the wording quoted here should not be cited for any as_of before 2023-11-26.
Says nothing about which fintech companies a16z declined or how its fintech investments performed.

items.title: Investing in Stitch
items.published_at_basis: Page displays 'Posted May 13, 2026'. Page JSON-LD datePublished is 2026-05-14T05:55:55+00:00 (likely the evening of May 13 in US Pacific time; not confirmed).
items.available_at_basis: Conservative: the later of the displayed date (2026-05-13) and the UTC date of the JSON-LD datePublished timestamp (2026-05-14). Earliest Wayback capture is 2026-05-15T01:55:15Z.
items.thesis: a16z argues that core banking systems of record are so hard to replace (it names FIS and Fiserv in the United States) that financial institutions sit on decades of infrastructure debt, which it calls the single biggest obstacle to AI adoption. It backs Stitch, an API-first core banking and operations platform starting in the Middle East, which a16z calls a rare greenfield opportunity: it says Saudi Arabia plans to add hundreds of new financial institutions that need core banking software for the first time. Traction figures are reported by a16z, not independently verified.
items.thesis_review: Reviewed by Yaseen (2026-11-13): Checked on 2026-11-13 against the live page and the archive capture: all 4 quotes appear verbatim on both. Thesis substance confirmed; edited for precision only: FIS and Fiserv are named as U.S. examples; 'banks' widened to 'financial institutions' as on the page; the 'need core software for the first time' point is attributed to the Saudi Arabia plan the page cites, not the whole Middle East. Hypotheses unchanged (labelled curator-derived). Quote kinds: all 4 confirmed as classified. The $5 billion and 10x/20x figures are documentary_fact only in the sense that a16z reports them; they are unaudited and have no base values. Limitation: this checks the summary against the page text only.
hypotheses: Curator-derived, not a firm claim: legacy systems of record are the binding constraint on AI adoption in banking, because agents need clean APIs and data.
Curator-derived, not a firm claim: replacing a core system is easiest where there is no incumbent yet (greenfield institutions), not at established banks.

quotes.text: The result of this incumbency is that financial institutions are sitting on decades of infrastructure debt. This debt has become the single biggest obstacle to AI adoption.
In the last six months alone, more than $5 billion has been transacted on the Stitch platform.
quotes.note: Company metric as reported by the investor; not independently verified and the six-month window is not dated on the page.

quotes.text: Customer numbers grew 10x in 2025, revenue grew 20x, and Stitch has seen pull beyond the GCC into Africa and Southeast Asia.
quotes.note: Growth multiples as reported by the investor; base values not disclosed.

quotes.text: We are thrilled to lead Stitch’s Series A — and honored to make this our first investment in Saudi Arabia.
quotes.note: Deal fact: a16z leads the Series A. Round size is not stated on the page.

limitations: Investment announcements are persuasive writing by an interested party, not calibrated forecasts.
Traction metrics are self-reported and have no stated base values or audit.
One announced investment says nothing about deals a16z declined or about returns.
Not usable for any as_of before 2026-05-14.

items.title: Partnering with Etched: Building the Inference Machine
items.available_at_basis: Displayed publication date; corroborated by a Wayback capture on the same day (2026-07-23T19:13:59Z).
items.thesis: Sequoia argues inference is on the path to becoming the largest market in the world and that the intelligence race is fundamentally compute constrained. It backs Etched's inference-specific hardware while naming the core difficulty: novel hardware is among the hardest things to get right while models change every few weeks, so winning means iterating fast enough to keep pace with the models. Sequoia says it is backing the team's ability to keep shipping new generations ('the machine that builds the machine'), not only its first chip. It is leading Etched's $300M Series C at a $10B pre-money valuation.
items.thesis_review: Reviewed by Yaseen (2026-11-13): Checked on 2026-11-13 against the live page and the archive capture: all 5 quotes appear verbatim on both. Thesis edited: 'a very large market' understated the page ('on the path to becoming the largest market in the world'); 'hardware takes a long time to build' is not on the page (it says novel hardware is 'among the hardest things in the world to get right'), and the page does not call this 'the main risk'; the curator inference that the round size 'shows how capital intensive the bet is' was removed, leaving the deal terms as stated; the page's stated reason for investing (the team's ability to keep shipping generations) was added. First hypothesis: removed the 'not model capability' contrast, which the page does not draw. Quote kinds: all 5 confirmed as classified; 'We expect it will do very well in the market' stays analyst_interpretation because it has no number, target or date. Limitation: this checks the summary against the page text only.
hypotheses: Curator-derived, not a firm claim: compute supply is a binding constraint on AI progress and deployment.
Curator-derived, not a firm claim: fast-changing model architectures are a key risk for specialized hardware, so the ability to iterate quickly matters more than any single chip generation.

quotes.text: We are delighted to be partnering with Etched and leading their $300 Million Series C at a $10 Billion pre-money valuation, joined by our friends at Jane Street, Andreessen Horowitz, Diffusion, and SK Hynix.
quotes.note: Deal terms as stated by the lead investor.

quotes.text: Earlier this year, Etched taped out its first generation chip at TSMC, making it the first post-ChatGPT-era company with a successful full-reticle A0 chip tape-out on TSMC’s leading-edge nodes.
quotes.note: Investor-relayed company claim ('first' is not independently verified).

quotes.text: Novel computing hardware is among the hardest things in the world to get right, and the ground underneath is constantly moving. Models change every few weeks, context lengths stretch, attention gets reinvented, the mix of dense and sparse keeps shifting.
quotes.note: Risk framing: model uncertainty for hardware.

quotes.text: The intelligence race is fundamentally compute constrained.
Etched has built a beautiful machine in Gen 1. We expect it will do very well in the market.
quotes.note: A forward-looking but non-numeric expectation with no target or date; not a quantitative testable forecast.

limitations: Published 2026-07-23: unusable for any replay with as_of before that date.
Investment announcement by the lead investor: persuasive writing, not a calibrated forecast. Contains no quantitative testable forecast.
Says nothing about deals Sequoia declined or about returns.
Sequoia notes Andreessen Horowitz also participated; this is not an independent second opinion from a16z.

items.title: The State of AI 2025
items.published_at_basis: Page displays 'Published on Aug 13, 2025' and 'Published08/13/2025'. No machine-readable date found in the page HTML.
items.available_at_basis: Displayed publication date; corroborated by a Wayback capture on the same day (2025-08-13T21:24:01Z).
items.thesis: Bessemer argues AI is moving enterprise software from systems of record to 'systems of action' that act on data, and that the switching-cost moats of legacy systems of record are degrading. It also warns that some fast AI growth is fragile: retention can be fragile when switching costs are low, competition is at an all-time high, and the ten 'Supernova' startups it surveyed average only about 25% gross margins. It holds up 'Shooting Stars' (which retain and expand customers, with about 60% gross margins) as the more important benchmark for founders. It predicts that private, grounded, trusted evaluations will make enterprise deployment '10x' (no metric or baseline is given), and expects incumbents to buy their way into AI through M&A.
items.thesis_review: Reviewed by Yaseen (2026-11-13): Checked on 2026-11-13 against the live page and the archive capture: all 6 quotes appear verbatim on both. Thesis edited: the earlier text left out the report's counterpoint that 'Shooting Stars' (about 60% gross margins; they retain and expand customers), not Supernovas, are the benchmark founders should aim for, which made the summary more negative than the page; the Supernova sample size (ten startups) and the page's word 'degrading' for moats were added; 'weak retention' softened to the page's 'retention can be fragile'; the deployment prediction now carries its '10x' and the missing metric; the M&A expectation was added because it is quoted. Hypotheses unchanged (labelled curator-derived). Quote kinds: all 6 confirmed as classified. Added scorable: false with scorable_reason at item level for the '10x' quantitative_forecast. Limitation: this checks the summary against the page text only; the benchmarks are self-reported by Bessemer.
hypotheses: Curator-derived, not a firm claim: hypergrowth revenue with low switching costs and thin gross margins is less durable than slower growth with strong retention and healthy margins.
Curator-derived, not a firm claim: AI lowers migration costs off legacy systems of record, weakening incumbents' switching-cost moats.
Curator-derived, not a firm claim: trusted, use-case-specific evaluation is a gating factor for enterprise AI deployment.

quotes.text: At Bessemer, we’ve already deployed over $1 billion in capital to AI-native startups since our initial commitment in 2023.
On average, these AI Supernovas have only 25% gross margins, often trading distribution for profit in the short term.
quotes.note: Self-reported average over the ten 'Supernova' startups Bessemer says it surveyed; not independently verifiable.

quotes.text: Retention can be fragile, especially when switching costs are low.
We feel we’re at the start of a once-in-a-generation shift—from systems of record to systems of action.
That’s why 2025–2026 will mark a turning point: AI evals will go private, grounded, and trusted—and enterprise deployment will 10x because of it.
quotes.note: Has a number (10x) and a time window (2025–2026), but no defined metric, baseline, or resolution source, so it cannot be scored as stated. Not scored by FAULTLINE. Marked not scorable in the item-level scorable and scorable_reason fields.

quotes.text: In 2025 and 2026, we expect to see a surge in M&A activity as incumbents move aggressively to buy their way into the AI era.
quotes.note: Directional expectation with no numeric threshold.

items.scorable_reason: Applies to the one quantitative_forecast quote ('enterprise deployment will 10x', 2025–2026): it does not say what 'enterprise deployment' measures, from what baseline, or what source would show whether it happened, so it cannot be resolved or scored as stated. FAULTLINE does not score it. Stored at item level because the API's quote schema does not accept extra quote fields.
limitations: Published 2025-08-13: exclude from replays with as_of before that date.
Research marketing by an investor with portfolio exposure; the page's own disclaimer says certain companies discussed may be current or former Bessemer portfolio companies.
Benchmarks come from a sample chosen by the firm ('20 high-growth, durable AI startups across our portfolio and beyond'); not a representative or audited dataset.
Predictions are persuasive writing; none is scored by FAULTLINE, and none has an explicit resolution source.
Says nothing about deals Bessemer declined or about returns.
